docs.title: Start with MeshCore
docs.text:
Pick the guide that matches what you want the device to do:

  • Send and receive messages with a companion.
  • Improve local coverage with a repeater.
  • Host a persistent room with a room server.
  • Share data with CoreScope with an observer.

Not sure which one fits? Compare the roles.

docs.title: Before setup
docs.text: Check the community directory for local radio settings. If none are listed, use the Canada defaults. Each setup guide covers preparation, configuration, and a quick working check.

docs.title: Choose a MeshCore role
docs.text:
Choose a role based on the job the device will do.

Role Use it for Relays mesh traffic? Usually Setup Companion Send and receive messages Normally no Mobile; often pairs with a phone Set up a companion Repeater Improve local coverage Yes Fixed with continuous power Set up a repeater Room server Keep a shared room available Can, but not recommended Fixed with continuous power Set up a room server Observer Send heard network data to CoreScope No Fixed; requirements vary Set up an observer

docs.title: Role details
docs.text:
Companion nodes are the small personal devices (handheld or portable) that let a user connect to the mesh.

  • Run on battery or USB power.
  • Usually pair with a smartphone over Bluetooth for messaging.
  • Standalone options like the T-Deck include a screen and keyboard, but we don't recommend them for beginners since the firmware is still rough.
  • Normally do not route packets. Client repeat is a limited off-grid feature; leave it off on an established public mesh unless local guidance says otherwise.

Repeaters are fixed installations, typically mounted at elevation (rooftop, tower, mast), that extend range and link mesh segments.

  • Run continuously on mains or solar power. Most Ottawa repeaters operate on solar.
  • Form the recommended routing backbone for an established mesh.

Room servers run specialized firmware that functions like a persistent chat room or mini-BBS.

  • When a companion connects, it can retrieve up to 32 unseen messages, similar to checking an inbox.
  • Can repeat, but this is not recommended. Ottawa keeps repeat disabled on room servers and uses separate repeaters.
  • Lack several repeater and remote-administration features. Use them as shared message rooms, not as network repeaters.

New to MeshCore? Start with a companion. Before buying or flashing, confirm that the setup guide supports your device.

If none of these roles fits, ask the community before buying hardware.

docs.title: Start with a companion
docs.text:
A companion is a personal messaging device. It does not route traffic for other users. Most pair with an app; some have their own screen and controls.

Install and configure a companion

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Check the recommended companion options.
  • Confirm the detailed flashing guide lists your device.
  • Use a data-capable USB cable and a supported browser.
  • Record any identity or settings you need before following an erase step.

docs.title: Know what flashing changes
docs.text: The linked flashing guide replaces the device firmware and configures it as a companion. Stop before erasing if you cannot recover information you need.

docs.title: Flash the companion
docs.text: Follow Flash and configure a companion.

docs.title: Use the right radio settings
docs.text:
Use USA/Canada (Recommended) with the 3-byte path setting unless your community lists different settings.

Match your local mesh

Check the community directory. If your community publishes different settings, use those settings instead.

Reboot after changing the radio settings, then send an advert.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
The companion is ready when:

  1. the device shows the Canada settings or your community's settings; and
  2. a nearby known-good device or community member can see its advert.

Use the companion verification checklist.

docs.title: Setup checklist
docs.text:
Checks are saved only in this browser.

  1. Confirm compatible hardware
  2. Back up and prepare
  3. Follow the flashing guide
  4. Apply Canada or local settings
  5. Check the device nearby
  6. Test with another mesh user

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Keep the local settings recorded and check them again after firmware changes. Use MeshCore how-to guides for common messaging tasks. Find your community, then exchange a test message with a nearby user. If nobody can see the advert, get help.

docs.title: Get help
docs.text:
Start with the symptom. Do not post passwords, private keys, precise locations, or unredacted command output.

What is wrong? Start here You are unsure which role or hardware fits Compare roles A nearby device cannot see your advert Recheck the verification steps and local settings You need local settings or another person to test Find a community An observer is missing or has no recent activity Observer troubleshooting You need a common MeshCore answer MeshCore FAQ A page is missing or incorrect Share an idea

docs.title: Ask the community
docs.text:
• MeshCore Canada forum — searchable public discussions and support.
  • MeshCore Canada Discord — live community chat.

Include:

  • the device role and model;
  • the guide and step where you stopped;
  • what you expected;
  • what happened instead;
  • the Canada or local setting name, without secrets;
  • any error text after removing sensitive values.

docs.title: Stop before retrying when
docs.text:
• the next step would erase data you have not backed up;
  • the hardware is hot, damaged, wet, or wired unexpectedly;
  • you would lose the only way to reach a remote node;
  • a local operator says the proposed settings conflict with the mesh.

docs.title: Try one change at a time
docs.text: Return to Check your setup after making one change. Testing one change at a time makes the result easier to understand.

docs.title: Start with an observer
docs.text:
An observer listens through a MeshCore radio and sends network data to CoreScope. Observing does not require repeating; a node can do both if configured for it. Observers can run on radio firmware, an always-on computer, or a home-automation host.

Read what the service collects and who can access it before enabling an observer.

Choose an observer setup

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Open the observer method chooser.
  • Pick a method that matches the radio, operating system, and host you already have.
  • Back up configuration before replacing firmware or installing a service.
  • Use a real nearby location code when the chosen method asks for one.

docs.title: What setup changes
docs.text: Depending on the method, setup may replace radio firmware, install a host service, or add a home-automation integration. It also enables public network data publishing.

docs.title: Set up the observer
docs.text: Use the observer method chooser, then follow only the guide for the selected method.

docs.title: Use the right radio settings
docs.text:
The connected radio must use the same settings as the nearby mesh. Start with USA/Canada (Recommended) and the 3-byte path setting unless your community lists different settings.

Match your local mesh

Check the community directory. A connected observer can be online while hearing no useful traffic if its radio settings do not match nearby devices.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
The observer is working when:

  1. its radio hears known nearby mesh activity;
  2. it appears in CoreScope Observers; and
  3. recent activity appears after a nearby transmission.

Use the observer verification checklist.

docs.title: Setup checklist
docs.text:
Checks are saved only in this browser.

  1. Read what observer data becomes public
  2. Choose a supported observer method
  3. Back up and prepare
  4. Follow the selected setup guide
  5. Apply local radio and service settings
  6. Check that the radio hears nearby activity
  7. Find the observer in CoreScope

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Check the observer after radio, network, credential, host, or firmware changes. Open Check your observer for the detailed health view. If it is missing or quiet, get help.

docs.title: Start with a repeater
docs.text:
A repeater extends coverage by routing traffic for other users. Because it is fixed infrastructure, plan its power, antenna, access, and maintenance before installation.

Install and configure a repeater

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Check recommended repeater options.
  • Agree on the site and settings with the local community.
  • Keep physical recovery access while testing.
  • Record the current identity and settings before any erase or update.

docs.title: Know what flashing changes
docs.text: The guide installs repeater firmware and sets radio, identity, adverts, and regional settings. Test on the bench before a difficult installation.

docs.title: Flash the repeater
docs.text: Follow Flash and configure a repeater.

docs.title: Use the right radio and region settings
docs.text:
Use USA/Canada (Recommended) with the 3-byte path setting unless your community lists different settings.

Coordinate before installation

Check the community directory. Nearby repeaters need matching local settings, and operators should agree on changes that affect shared traffic.

Use the repeater configurator to find the regional settings and review its commands before applying them.

JavaScript is required for the live duplicate-ID check. You can also [search the public-key prefix in CoreScope](https://live.meshcore.ca/#/nodes).

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
The repeater is ready to install when:

  1. it keeps the intended settings after a reboot;
  2. it sends an advert; and
  3. a nearby known-good companion receives that advert.

Use the repeater verification checklist.

docs.title: Setup checklist
docs.text:
Checks are saved only in this browser.

  1. Confirm compatible hardware and site
  2. Back up and prepare
  3. Follow the flashing guide
  4. Apply local and regional settings
  5. Bench-check the repeater
  6. Test with a nearby companion

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Keep a record of the site, owner, recovery access, settings, and last successful check. Recheck it after firmware, antenna, power, or region changes. For firmware 1.14 or newer, review the coordinated loop-detection setting before changing a community repeater.

Review antenna and mounting guidance before final installation. If a check fails, get help.

docs.title: Start with a room server
docs.text:
A room server keeps a shared room available. It does not replace a repeater; use a repeater for routing and coverage.

Install and configure a room server

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Confirm the flasher offers room-server firmware for the device.
  • Decide who will maintain the room and retain recovery access.
  • Record any identity or settings you need before following an erase step.
  • Prepare separate guest and administrator credentials.

docs.title: Know what flashing changes
docs.text: The linked guide replaces the firmware and sets room-server identity, access credentials, and radio settings.

docs.title: Flash the room server
docs.text: Follow Flash and configure a room server. Use that guide for device selection, flashing, access setup, and recovery.

docs.title: Use the right radio settings
docs.text:
Use USA/Canada (Recommended) with the 3-byte path setting unless your community lists different settings.

Match your local mesh

Check the community directory. If your community publishes different settings, use those settings instead.

Keep administrator credentials private. Share only the guest access information intended for room users.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
The room server is ready when:

  1. a nearby companion discovers its advert;
  2. the companion can enter with the guest credentials; and
  3. the administrator can still recover and maintain it.

Use the room-server verification checklist.

docs.title: Setup checklist
docs.text:
Checks are saved only in this browser.

  1. Confirm compatible hardware
  2. Back up and prepare
  3. Follow the flashing guide
  4. Apply access and local settings
  5. Check the room server nearby
  6. Test discovery and guest access

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Record who maintains the room and how users get support. Ask a nearby community member to test it from a second companion. Recheck discovery and guest access after firmware, credential, or radio-setting changes. If discovery or access fails, get help.

docs.title: Check your setup
docs.text:
A powered-on device or a connected status does not mean setup is finished. Use the check for your device below.

Before testing, confirm the device still shows the Canada settings or your community's settings.

docs.title: Companion
docs.text:
1. Reboot after the last radio-setting change.
  2. Send an advert.
  3. Ask a nearby user with a known-good device to confirm that the advert appears.
  4. Exchange a test message when another user is available.

The companion is ready

A nearby known-good device sees the advert, and the two devices can exchange a test message.

If the advert is missing, compare radio and path settings before reflashing.

docs.title: Repeater
docs.text:
1. Keep the repeater accessible on the bench.
  2. Reboot it and confirm the intended settings remain.
  3. Send an advert from the repeater.
  4. Confirm a nearby known-good companion receives it.
  5. Repeat the check after any antenna, power, or installation change.

The repeater is ready

The repeater retains its settings and a nearby known-good companion receives its advert.

Keep it off hard-to-reach spots until the bench check passes.

docs.title: Room server
docs.text:
1. Reboot the room server.
  2. Send its advert.
  3. Confirm a nearby companion discovers it.
  4. Enter using the guest credentials.
  5. Confirm the administrator still has maintenance access.

The room server is ready

A companion discovers the room and guest access works without exposing the administrator credentials.

docs.title: Observer
docs.text:
1. Create nearby mesh activity with a known-good device.
  2. Confirm the observer radio is using matching settings.
  3. Open CoreScope Observers.
  4. Find your observer and check for recent activity.
  5. Use Check your observer for the full health checklist.

The observer is working

Your observer appears in CoreScope and shows recent activity after a nearby transmission.

An online broker connection alone is not the final check.

docs.title: If a check fails
docs.text: If the check passes, you're done. If it does not, get help and describe what was missing.

docs.title: Network tools
docs.text:
Choose the tool that matches your task.

  • Configure a repeater

    Build region commands for a repeater after choosing its location.

    Open the repeater configurator

  • Find your MeshCore region

    Search a place or use the map to see its Canadian MeshCore region.

    Find my region

  • View the live network

    View public observers, packets, nodes, and map data in CoreScope.

    Open CoreScope (external)

  • Set up an observer

    Choose an observer method, then check that packets appear in CoreScope.

    Choose an observer method

docs.title: Before setting up an observer
docs.text:
Observers publish heard packet data. Read what is collected and who can access it before setting one up.

Need help? See observer troubleshooting or ask the community.

docs.title: MeshCore Canada
docs.text:
Bienvenue! Nous améliorons activement ce site. Vous avez trouvé quelque chose de difficile à comprendre ou de désuet? Signalez-le sur GitHub.

Réseau illustratif · Sources cartographiques

docs.text:

    Commencer la configuration guidée

docs.title: Paramètres radio par défaut au Canada
docs.text:
Utilisez ces paramètres, sauf si votre communauté en indique d’autres.

Paramètre Valeur par défaut au Canada Préréglage radio USA/Canada (Recommended) Valeurs radio détaillées 910.525 MHz / 62.5 kHz / SF7 / CR5 Hachage des chemins 3 octets Commande correspondante set path.hash.mode 2

Prévu : un préréglage Canada distinct, avec les mêmes paramètres radio que USA/Canada et un hachage de 3 octets par défaut pour tous les types d’appareils. Suivre la discussion.

docs.title: Améliorer MeshCore Canada
docs.text: Quelque chose manque ou porte à confusion? Partagez une idée ou mettez à jour une communauté.

docs.title: À propos du projet
docs.text: MeshCore Canada est un projet communautaire indépendant. Apprenez-en plus ou contribuez au projet.

docs.title: À propos de MeshCore Canada
docs.text:
MeshCore Canada est un projet communautaire destiné aux personnes qui utilisent MeshCore au Canada. Nous maintenons des guides de configuration, un répertoire des communautés, les données des régions canadiennes et des liens vers les outils partagés.

MeshCore Canada est indépendant du projet MeshCore officiel. Pour en savoir plus sur le micrologiciel, les applications et le protocole, consultez la documentation officielle de MeshCore.

docs.title: Ce que nous maintenons
docs.text:
• des guides de configuration, de matériel et de dépannage;
  • le répertoire des communautés canadiennes et la carte des régions;
  • des outils pour les répéteurs et les observateurs;
  • le code source du site Web.

Nous exploitons aussi des services MQTT et CoreScope partagés pour les utilisateurs canadiens. Ces services sont maintenus par Mr. Alderson, Ded, n30nex et Kranic.

docs.title: Participer
docs.text:
• Trouvez une communauté canadienne pour connaître ses paramètres et ses coordonnées.
  • Obtenez de l’aide si une configuration ou une vérification du réseau échoue.
  • Partagez une idée ou signalez un problème.
  • Contribuez sur GitHub.

Ne publiez jamais de clés privées, de mots de passe, d’emplacements privés précis ni d’autres renseignements sensibles dans un formulaire, un billet GitHub, un forum ou une conversation.

docs.title: Contribuer à MeshCore Canada
docs.text:
Choisissez la façon dont vous voulez aider. La plupart des options ne demandent aucune expérience avec Git ou GitHub.

  • Partager une idée

    Signalez quelque chose qui manque, porte à confusion ou est difficile à utiliser. Aucun compte GitHub n’est nécessaire.

    Partager une idée

  • Ajouter ou mettre à jour une communauté

    Indiquez le nom, la région, les coordonnées, la langue et les paramètres locaux de la communauté.

    Ajouter une communauté · Mettre à jour une communauté

  • Corriger une page

    Signalez une erreur factuelle, un lien brisé, une coquille ou une instruction difficile à comprendre.

    Signaler une correction

  • Proposer une modification de région

    Proposez une nouvelle région ou une modification de ses limites.

    Ouvrir l’éditeur de région

  • Contribuer sur GitHub

    Améliorez un guide ou travaillez sur un billet ouvert.

    Ouvrir le dépôt

Ne partagez aucun secret

Les soumissions sont publiques. Retirez les mots de passe, les jetons d’accès, les clés privées, les adresses privées, les coordonnées privées précises et les sorties de commande sensibles.

docs.title: Vous ne savez pas quoi choisir?
docs.text: Partagez une idée et nous vous aiderons à l’orienter.

docs.title: Confidentialité chez MeshCore Canada
docs.text: Vous pouvez consulter ce site sans compte MeshCore Canada ni compte GitHub.

docs.title: Quand des données quittent votre navigateur
docs.text: Action Données transmises Destination Rechercher dans cette documentation Vos mots de recherche restent dans le navigateur Nulle part Trouver des communautés à proximité La ville recherchée API Géolocalisateur de Ressources naturelles Canada; les distances sont calculées dans votre navigateur Charger les totaux du réseau dans l’en-tête Votre adresse IP et les renseignements habituels d’une requête Web, sans texte de recherche Beacon à dev.meshcore.ca Rechercher un lieu dans les outils de région Le lieu, le code d’aéroport ou le code postal saisi Vérification locale d’abord, puis OpenStreetMap ou geocoder.ca au besoin Ouvrir la carte interactive des régions Votre adresse IP et la partie visible de la carte OpenStreetMap Vérifier un identifiant de parcours de répéteur Le premier octet de la clé publique Beacon à dev.meshcore.ca; les comparaisons régionales et des préfixes plus longs restent dans votre navigateur Charger le nombre d’étoiles GitHub Votre adresse IP et les renseignements habituels d’une requête Web GitHub Ouvrir un lien externe Les renseignements habituels d’une requête Web Le service externe indiqué Soumettre une idée ou une proposition de région Le texte et les détails affichés lors de la révision, ainsi que la vérification antipourriel Le service de soumission de MeshCore Canada, Cloudflare Turnstile et un billet GitHub public

docs.title: Soumissions publiques
docs.text:
Les idées et les propositions de limites deviennent des billets GitHub publics. Relisez l’aperçu avant de soumettre. N’incluez aucun mot de passe, aucune clé privée, aucune adresse résidentielle, aucune coordonnée privée ni aucun autre renseignement personnel.

Le service de soumission peut conserver des journaux de sécurité et de limitation du débit. Aucune période de conservation n’a encore été publiée.

docs.title: Données enregistrées sur votre appareil
docs.text:
Changer de langue ou passer entre la carte et le configurateur conserve votre sélection dans l’URL de destination. Elle peut contenir les coordonnées saisies, un lieu, des chemins régionaux et un profil radio. Ces URL peuvent apparaître dans l’historique du navigateur et les journaux du serveur. Ne partagez pas un lien qui contient un emplacement privé. Les résumés téléchargés omettent les coordonnées exactes et les identifiants de connexion.

Les listes de configuration, les brouillons d’idées et le dernier code de région Beacon choisi dans l’outil de vérification sont enregistrés uniquement dans votre navigateur lorsque vous utilisez ces fonctions. Les clés publiques des répéteurs, les mots de passe, les clés privées, les jetons antipourriel et les recherches d’emplacement n’y sont pas enregistrés.

Les totaux de l’en-tête sont mis en cache pendant cinq minutes dans l’onglet courant. La ville recherchée dans le répertoire apparaît dans l’URL pour partager ou retrouver les résultats.

Vous pouvez effacer les données enregistrées par ce site dans les paramètres de votre navigateur. Le formulaire d’idée offre aussi l’action Effacer le brouillon enregistré.

docs.title: Services externes
docs.text: CoreScope, les services MQTT, les outils de reprogrammation et les sites communautaires ont leurs propres responsables et politiques de confidentialité.

docs.title: Mesure d’audience
docs.text: MeshCore Canada n’utilise aucun outil d’analyse d’audience.

docs.title: Questions ou corrections
docs.text: Signalez une correction liée à la confidentialité sans compte GitHub ou ouvrez un billet sur GitHub.

docs.title: Partager une idée
docs.text:
Partagez une idée ou signalez un problème. Aucun compte GitHub n’est nécessaire.

Ce formulaire est public. N’incluez aucun mot de passe, aucune clé, aucune adresse ni aucune coordonnée privée.

  1. 1RelireVérifier ce qui sera public
  2. 2VérifierPasser la vérification antipourriel
  3. 3SoumettreCréer le billet public
JavaScript est désactivé. Continuez sur GitHub; un compte sera nécessaire. Corrigez ces champs Décrivez votre idée

Ajoutez un titre et décrivez le problème ou l’idée. Le reste est facultatif.
